About Helix Grid

Helix Grid Operations Console

Helix Grid is a fictional real-time observability console for a six-region renewable-energy network — the kind of always-on, streaming, stateful interface that a network operations center watches around the clock. Everything you see is generated live in your browser; there is no server.

Live data engine

A simulated streaming source ticks once per second of grid time — demand waves, a diurnal solar curve, generation mix, frequency, market price and per-service latency, all with realistic noise.

Hand-drawn charts

Scrolling time-series, a stacked generation-mix area, sparklines, radial gauges, bar charts and a 144-node substation heatmap — every pixel painted on canvas and SVG, zero chart libraries.

Incident simulation

Spontaneous and operator-triggered incidents ripple through the charts, spike the right service, flood the event log and raise an alert banner — then auto-resolve and log their MTTR.

What you're looking at

The console models a renewable operator coordinating six control areas — Pacific NW, California, ERCOT Texas, Midwest, New England and the Southeast — across roughly 25 GW of nameplate capacity. The operator's job is to keep generation matched to demand within a razor-thin frequency band around 60.00 Hz, dispatch storage and reserves, and keep the software platform (SCADA gateway, dispatch engine, forecast ML, settlement API and more) healthy.

How the simulation works

  • A small xorshift RNG plus layered sine waves produce believable trends, daily seasonality and Gaussian noise — no two sessions look the same.
  • The engine keeps fixed-length ring buffers per metric so charts open already full and scroll smoothly as new ticks arrive.
  • A requestAnimationFrame scheduler advances sim time, honoring your play-speed (0.25×–8×) and pause state, and catches up if a tab was backgrounded.
  • Charts redraw every animation frame for smoothness while KPIs, bars and the heatmap update once per simulated tick.
  • Incidents have a severity, a lifetime and a blast radius — they bias the affected service's latency and error rate and the matching region's stress until they resolve.

Controls & persistence

  • Pause / Resume the feed — or press Space.
  • Simulate incident to inject a fault — or press I. If one is already open it escalates to SEV-1.
  • Time window (30s–4m), region filter, and play speed on the overview control bar.
  • Log severity chips and a free-text filter on the event stream.
  • Theme toggle (dark / light).

Your theme, paused state, play speed, time window, region selection and log filters all persist to localStorage under helix.prefs.v1, so the console comes back exactly how you left it.
